findings.body: The special Roll-over state is recognized only when the same result also contains `budget.state === "no_gl_line"`. A valid selection such as Actual plus Roll-over grouped by GL need not request Budget, yet an Actual-only GL still has no Roll-over leaf. Under loaded coverage this schema rejects the truthful `No Roll-over line for this GL` state and instead requires a numeric Roll-over, so the supported selection cannot preserve that Actual row without inventing a balance. Infer the special state from the GL grouping/state itself rather than requiring an unrequested Budget value, and change the Roll-over-only regression case to succeed.
findings.title: Not done: Roll-over-only GL results can represent missing source lines

findings.body: The catalog combination refinement checks duplicates and dimension compatibility but not the selection schema's measure rules. It therefore accepts combinations such as `measureIds: ["actual", "percentage"]`, although no corresponding selection can pass: percentage requires `actual_vs_budget`, and that comparison requires both Actual and Budget unless percentage is the only returned measure. The catalog can consequently advertise an unusable “valid combination.” Apply the same comparison dependency to catalog combinations and add malformed catalog cases for Actual+percentage and Budget+percentage.
findings.title: Not done: catalog combinations match accepted selections

findings.body: Rows are checked individually, but no invariant makes their selected dimension coordinates unique. For a GL-grouped result, two rows with different opaque `key` values and the same `dimensions.gl` both validate, allowing the strict result boundary to accept repeated GL aggregates—the exact fan-out shape this story must prevent. Reject duplicate coordinate tuples (and duplicate row keys) and add a negative result-validation case.
findings.title: Not done: result validation rejects duplicate aggregate coordinates
